questions.q: The sternal angle (angle of Louis) lies at the manubriosternal junction and serves as the surface landmark for which costal cartilage?
questions.explain: The sternal angle (manubriosternal joint) lies directly opposite the second costal cartilage, providing the standard anatomical starting point for counting ribs and intercostal spaces on the anterior chest wall.

open.q: Which costal cartilage articulates with the sternum at the level of the sternal angle (angle of Louis)?

questions.q: To which intervertebral disc level does the horizontal plane passing through the sternal angle correspond posteriorly?
questions.explain: The transthoracic plane passes anteriorly through the sternal angle and posteriorly through the T4-T5 intervertebral disc, marking the boundary between the superior and inferior mediastinum, the tracheal bifurcation, and the start and end of the aortic arch.

open.q: Through which thoracic intervertebral disc level does the horizontal plane of the sternal angle pass posteriorly?

questions.q: In a normal adult, where is the apex beat of the heart palpated on the anterior chest wall?
options: Left 5th intercostal space, just medial to the midclavicular line (about 9 cm from the midline)
Left 4th intercostal space, in the anterior axillary line
Right 5th intercostal space, at the parasternal border
Left 2nd intercostal space, lateral to the sternal margin
questions.explain: The cardiac apex (formed by the inferolateral tip of the left ventricle) produces the apex beat in the left 5th intercostal space roughly 9 cm from the midsternal line, just medial to the midclavicular line.

open.q: State the normal surface location of the cardiac apex beat on the anterior thoracic wall.
accept: left 5th intercostal space medial to midclavicular line

questions.q: Where is the stethoscope placed to best auscultate the aortic valve without interference from overlying bony structures?
options: Right 2nd intercostal space at the sternal margin
Left 2nd intercostal space at the sternal margin
Left 5th intercostal space at the midclavicular line
Left 4th or 5th intercostal space at the lower left sternal border
questions.explain: Although the aortic valve lies behind the left half of the sternum at the 3rd intercostal space, its sound is transmitted upward along the ascending aorta to the right 2nd intercostal space just lateral to the sternum.

open.q: In which intercostal space and on which side of the sternum is the aortic valve best auscultated?

questions.q: Along the midaxillary line, what are the inferior surface margins of the visceral pleura (lung) and the parietal pleura during quiet respiration?
options: Lung at rib 8; parietal pleura at rib 10
Lung at rib 6; parietal pleura at rib 8
Lung at rib 10; parietal pleura at rib 12
Lung at rib 4; parietal pleura at rib 6
questions.explain: The inferior borders of the lung and parietal pleura follow the 6-8-10 and 8-10-12 rule: at the midclavicular line (ribs 6 and 8), midaxillary line (ribs 8 and 10), and scapular line (ribs 10 and 12).

open.q: At the midaxillary line, which ribs mark the inferior border of the lung and the inferior reflection of the parietal pleura respectively?

questions.q: A 26-year-old man requires an emergency tube thoracostomy (chest tube insertion) in the 'safe triangle' of the lateral chest wall. Which anatomical landmark forms the inferior horizontal border of this safe triangle so the diaphragm and liver/spleen are avoided?
options: Horizontal line at the level of the nipple (5th intercostal space)
questions.explain: The safe triangle for intercostal drain insertion is bounded anteriorly by the lateral border of pectoralis major, posteriorly by the anterior border of latissimus dorsi, and inferiorly by a horizontal line at the level of the nipple (5th intercostal space).

open.q: Which intercostal space corresponds to the horizontal inferior boundary of the safe triangle for chest tube insertion?

questions.q: The transpyloric plane (Addison plane) lies midway between the jugular (suprasternal) notch and the upper border of the pubic symphysis, passing posteriorly through which vertebral level?
questions.explain: The transpyloric plane passes through the lower border of the L1 vertebra (roughly a handbreadth below the xiphisternal joint) and intersects the pylorus, fundus of the gallbladder (tip of right 9th costal cartilage), renal hila, and origin of the superior mesenteric artery.

open.q: Through which lumbar vertebral level does the transpyloric plane pass posteriorly?

questions.q: Which surface landmark corresponds to the fundus of the gallbladder on the anterior abdominal wall?
options: Tip of the right 9th costal cartilage where the linea semilunaris meets the costal margin
questions.explain: The fundus of the gallbladder lies at the intersection of the right lateral vertical (midclavicular/semilunar) line and the right costal margin at the tip of the 9th costal cartilage, which is where Murphy sign is elicited.

open.q: At the tip of which costal cartilage does the fundus of the gallbladder contact the anterior abdominal wall?

questions.q: McBurney point, the surface landmark overlying the base of the vermiform appendix, is located where?
options: One-third of the way along a line from the right anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus
Midway between the anterior superior iliac spine and the pubic symphysis
Two-thirds of the way from the right anterior superior iliac spine to the pubic tubercle
At the intersection of the transpyloric and right midclavicular lines
questions.explain: McBurney point lies at the junction of the lateral one-third and medial two-thirds of the spinoumbilical line drawn from the right anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus.

open.q: Define the exact surface location of McBurney point on the anterior abdominal wall.
accept: one-third of the distance from the right ASIS to the umbilicus
junction of lateral one-third and medial two-thirds of spinoumbilical line

questions.q: The supracristal plane connects the highest points of the left and right iliac crests and corresponds to which lumbar vertebral level, commonly used as a landmark for lumbar puncture?
questions.explain: The supracristal (intercristal/Tuffier) line crosses the L4 spinous process or the L4-L5 intervertebral space, lying safely below the adult conus medullaris (L1-L2) for lumbar puncture.

open.q: Which lumbar spinous process or intervertebral space is intersected by the supracristal plane joining the highest points of the iliac crests?

questions.q: Where is the deep inguinal ring projected onto the surface of the lower anterior abdominal wall?
options: 1.25 cm superior to the midpoint of the inguinal ligament
1.25 cm superolateral to the pubic tubercle
1.25 cm inferior to the midinguinal point
At the anterior superior iliac spine
questions.explain: The deep inguinal ring lies 1.25 cm (half an inch) above the midpoint of the inguinal ligament (halfway between the ASIS and pubic tubercle), whereas the femoral artery pulse is palpated at the midinguinal point (halfway between the ASIS and pubic symphysis).

open.q: Relative to the midpoint of the inguinal ligament, where is the surface projection of the deep inguinal ring located?
accept: 1.25 cm above the midpoint of the inguinal ligament
half an inch above the midpoint of the inguinal ligament
just superior to the midpoint of the inguinal ligament

questions.q: Where is the superficial temporal artery pulse most easily palpated on the side of the head?
options: Immediately anterior to the tragus of the auricle over the posterior root of the zygomatic arch
At the inferior border of the mandible anterior to the masseter
At the medial canthus of the eye
questions.explain: The superficial temporal artery ascends across the posterior root of the zygomatic process of the temporal bone directly anterior to the tragus of the ear, where its pulsation is readily palpable.

open.q: Where on the lateral aspect of the head is the pulsation of the superficial temporal artery palpated?
accept: in front of the tragus over the zygomatic arch

questions.q: Where is the facial artery pulse palpated as it enters the face?
options: At the inferior border of the mandible immediately anterior to the masseter muscle
Over the bridge of the nose
At the angle of the mandible behind the sternocleidomastoid
Below the middle of the clavicle
questions.explain: The facial artery winds around the inferior margin of the body of the mandible at the anteroinferior angle of the masseter muscle, where it can be compressed against bone to control facial bleeding.

open.q: Along which bony border and anterior to which muscle is the facial artery pulse palpated as it enters the face?
accept: inferior border of mandible anterior to masseter
lower border of mandible in front of masseter

questions.q: At which cervical vertebral level is the arch of the cricoid cartilage palpated in the anterior midline of the neck?
questions.explain: The cricoid cartilage lies at the C6 vertebral level, marking the pharyngoesophageal junction, laryngotracheal junction, entry of the inferior thyroid artery, and the site where the common carotid artery can be compressed against Chassaignac tubercle.

open.q: Which cervical vertebra lies directly posterior to the palpable arch of the cricoid cartilage?

questions.q: Where is the brachial artery pulse routinely palpated before applying a stethoscope bell for blood pressure measurement?
options: Medial to the tendon of biceps brachii in the cubital fossa
Lateral to the tendon of biceps brachii
Posterior to the medial epicondyle of the humerus
questions.explain: In the cubital fossa, the brachial artery descends immediately medial to the palpable tendon of the biceps brachii muscle and lateral to the median nerve.

open.q: Relative to the biceps brachii tendon in the cubital fossa, where is the brachial artery pulse palpated?
accept: just medial to biceps brachii tendon

questions.q: At the anterior wrist, the radial artery pulse is palpated immediately lateral to which tendon?
questions.explain: On the distal anterior radius, the radial artery lies superficially between the tendon of brachioradialis laterally and the tendon of flexor carpi radialis medially.

open.q: Lateral to which prominent wrist flexor tendon is the radial artery pulse palpated on the distal anterior forearm?

questions.q: Which peripheral nerve can be rolled and palpated directly behind the medial epicondyle of the humerus?
questions.explain: The ulnar nerve passes superficially through the cubital tunnel posterior to the medial epicondyle of the humerus ('funny bone'), making it readily palpable and susceptible to compression.

open.q: Name the nerve that is palpable in the groove posterior to the medial epicondyle of the humerus.

questions.q: Where is the femoral artery pulse palpated in the groin?
options: At the midinguinal point, midway between the anterior superior iliac spine and the pubic symphysis
Midway between the anterior superior iliac spine and the pubic tubercle
Immediately medial to the adductor longus tendon
questions.explain: The femoral artery enters the femoral triangle beneath the inguinal ligament at the midinguinal point (halfway between the ASIS and the pubic symphysis), lying medial to the femoral nerve and lateral to the femoral vein.

open.q: Between which two anterior bony pelvic landmarks is the midinguinal point located for palpating the femoral artery pulse?
accept: anterior superior iliac spine and pubic symphysis

questions.q: Behind which ankle landmark is the posterior tibial artery pulse palpated?
options: Midway between the posterior border of the medial malleolus and the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon
Over the head of the fibula
Between the first and second metatarsal bases on the dorsum of the foot
questions.explain: The posterior tibial artery curves inferiorly behind the medial malleolus deep to the flexor retinaculum, halfway between the medial malleolus and the medial border of the calcaneal tendon.

open.q: Relative to the medial malleolus and calcaneal tendon, where is the posterior tibial artery pulse palpated?
accept: midway between the medial malleolus and calcaneal tendon

questions.q: Where is the dorsalis pedis artery pulse palpated on the dorsum of the foot?
options: Lateral to the tendon of extensor hallucis longus over the tarsal bones
Medial to the tendon of tibialis anterior
Over the tuberosity of the fifth metatarsal
questions.explain: The dorsalis pedis artery (continuation of the anterior tibial artery) runs distally on the dorsum of the foot immediately lateral to the tendon of extensor hallucis longus toward the first intermetatarsal space.

open.q: Lateral to which extensor tendon on the dorsum of the foot is the dorsalis pedis artery pulse palpated?

questions.q: At the sternal angle, the costal cartilage of which rib articulates with the sternum?
questions.explain: The sternal angle is the palpable ridge at the manubriosternal joint. The second costal cartilage attaches here, so it is the starting point for counting ribs.

open.q: At the sternal angle, the costal cartilage of which rib articulates with the sternum?

questions.q: The sternal angle lies at the level of which intervertebral disc?
questions.explain: The sternal angle is at the T4/T5 disc. The same plane marks the carina, the start and end of the aortic arch and the azygos vein entering the superior vena cava.

open.q: The sternal angle lies at the level of which intervertebral disc?
accept: Between the fourth and fifth thoracic vertebrae

questions.q: In a healthy adult lying supine, where is the apex beat normally felt?
options: Left fifth intercostal space, midclavicular line
Left third intercostal space, midclavicular line
Left fifth intercostal space, anterior axillary line
Right fifth intercostal space, midclavicular line
questions.explain: The apex beat is the lowest and most lateral cardiac impulse and is normally in the left fifth intercostal space about 9 cm from the midline. Displacement suggests cardiomegaly.

open.q: In a healthy adult lying supine, where is the apex beat normally felt?
accept: 5th left space in the midclavicular line
Fifth left space about 9 cm from the midline

questions.q: The transpyloric plane lies at which vertebral level?
questions.explain: The transpyloric plane (of Addison) lies at L1, midway between the jugular notch and the pubic symphysis. It passes through the pylorus, the neck of the pancreas and the renal hila.

open.q: At which vertebral level does the transpyloric plane lie?
accept: Midway between the jugular notch and the pubic symphysis

questions.q: The fundus of the gallbladder is found where the lateral border of the right rectus abdominis meets which costal cartilage?
questions.explain: The fundus lies at the tip of the ninth costal cartilage on the transpyloric plane. Tenderness here on inspiration is the basis of Murphy sign.

open.q: The fundus of the gallbladder is found where the lateral border of the right rectus abdominis meets which costal cartilage?
accept: Tip of the ninth costal cartilage

questions.q: Which vertebra has the most prominent spinous process at the root of the neck in most people?
questions.explain: C7 is called the vertebra prominens because its long, non-bifid spinous process is easily seen and felt. It is a landmark for counting spinous processes.

open.q: Which vertebra has the most prominent spinous process at the root of the neck in most people?

questions.q: Which laryngeal cartilage is the only complete ring and lies at the level of the C6 vertebra?
questions.explain: The cricoid cartilage is palpable below the thyroid cartilage and marks the junction of the larynx with the trachea and of the pharynx with the oesophagus.

open.q: Which laryngeal cartilage is the only complete ring and lies at the level of the C6 vertebra?

questions.q: The body of the hyoid bone lies at the level of which cervical vertebra?
questions.explain: The hyoid body is at C3, the thyroid cartilage at C4 to C5 and the cricoid cartilage at C6.

open.q: The body of the hyoid bone lies at the level of which cervical vertebra?

questions.q: The facial artery pulse is felt where the artery crosses which bone at the anterior edge of masseter?
questions.explain: The facial artery winds over the lower border of the mandible just in front of masseter, where it can be compressed against bone.

open.q: The facial artery pulse is felt where the artery crosses which bone at the anterior edge of masseter?

questions.q: Where is the superficial temporal pulse felt?
questions.explain: The superficial temporal artery crosses the root of the zygomatic arch in front of the ear, where it is palpable against the temporal bone.

open.q: Where is the superficial temporal pulse felt?
accept: Over the root of the zygomatic arch
Just in front of the external acoustic meatus

questions.q: Where is the radial pulse most easily felt at the wrist?
options: Lateral to the tendon of flexor carpi radialis
Medial to the tendon of flexor carpi ulnaris
Between the tendons of palmaris longus and FCR
Over the head of the ulna
questions.explain: The radial artery lies on the distal radius just lateral to the tendon of flexor carpi radialis, where the bone gives firm support for palpation.

open.q: Where is the radial pulse most easily felt at the wrist?
accept: Over the distal radius on the thumb side
Just lateral to the flexor tendon on the thumb side

questions.q: Which vein is most often chosen for venepuncture in the cubital fossa?
questions.explain: The median cubital vein is large, superficial and fairly fixed. It joins the cephalic and basilic veins across the front of the elbow.

open.q: Which vein is most often chosen for venepuncture in the cubital fossa?
accept: Vein connecting the cephalic and basilic veins

questions.q: Which structure protects the brachial artery and median nerve from a needle passed through the median cubital vein?
questions.explain: The bicipital aponeurosis (lacertus fibrosus) lies between the median cubital vein and the deeper brachial artery and median nerve.

open.q: Which structure protects the brachial artery and median nerve from a needle passed through the median cubital vein?
accept: Fibrous expansion of the biceps tendon

questions.q: At which point in the cubital fossa is the brachial pulse palpated for blood pressure measurement?
questions.explain: The brachial artery lies just medial to the tendon of biceps brachii in the cubital fossa. The stethoscope is placed here when taking blood pressure.

open.q: At which point in the cubital fossa is the brachial pulse palpated for blood pressure measurement?
accept: On the ulnar side of the biceps tendon
Between the biceps tendon and the medial epicondyle

questions.q: A nurse injects into the buttock and the patient develops foot drop and sensory loss in the leg and foot. Into which quadrant was the injection most likely given?
questions.explain: The sciatic nerve runs through the lower medial part of the buttock. The upper lateral quadrant is the safe site for intramuscular injection.

open.q: A nurse injects into the buttock and the patient develops foot drop and sensory loss in the leg and foot. Into which quadrant was the injection most likely given?
accept: Medial and inferior part of the buttock

questions.q: Where is the dorsalis pedis pulse felt on the dorsum of the foot?
options: Medial to the tibialis anterior tendon
questions.explain: The dorsalis pedis artery lies just lateral to the tendon of extensor hallucis longus over the tarsal bones. Absence of this pulse can be normal in a few people.

open.q: Where is the dorsalis pedis pulse felt on the dorsum of the foot?
accept: Lateral to the great toe extensor tendon
Between the first and second metatarsals

questions.q: Where is the posterior tibial pulse felt?
questions.explain: The posterior tibial artery passes behind the medial malleolus, between the flexor digitorum longus and flexor hallucis longus tendons.

open.q: Where is the posterior tibial pulse felt?
accept: Between the medial malleolus and the Achilles tendon
Medial side of the ankle behind the bony prominence

questions.q: In the femoral triangle, where does the femoral vein lie relative to the femoral artery?
questions.explain: The femoral sheath contents from lateral to medial are the nerve, artery, vein, empty space and lymphatics (NAVEL). The vein is therefore medial to the artery.

open.q: In the femoral triangle, where does the femoral vein lie relative to the femoral artery?

questions.q: Foot drop after a tight plaster cast on the leg is due to compression of the common fibular nerve at which site?
questions.explain: The common fibular nerve winds round the neck of the fibula, where it is subcutaneous and easy to compress. Injury causes foot drop and loss of eversion.

open.q: Foot drop after a tight plaster cast on the leg is due to compression of the common fibular nerve at which site?
accept: Where it winds round the fibula
Upper lateral leg just below the knee

questions.q: Where is McBurney's point, the usual site of maximal tenderness in acute appendicitis?
options: Midpoint between the umbilicus and the pubic symphysis
One-third of the way from the ASIS to the umbilicus
Lateral border of rectus abdominis at the umbilical level
Midpoint of the line joining the ASISs
questions.explain: McBurney's point lies on the right side at the junction of the lateral third and medial two-thirds of the line from the anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus. It corresponds to the base of the appendix.

open.q: Where is McBurney's point, the usual site of maximal tenderness in acute appendicitis?
accept: Lateral third of the line from the ASIS to the umbilicus
One-third distance from the right ASIS to the umbilicus

questions.q: A line joining the highest points of the iliac crests passes through which vertebral level?
questions.explain: The intercristal (Tuffier) line crosses the L4 spinous process or the L4/L5 interspace. It is used to locate the lumbar puncture site.

open.q: A line joining the highest points of the iliac crests passes through which vertebral level?

questions.q: Why is a needle for lumbar puncture in an adult inserted at L3/L4 or L4/L5 rather than at upper lumbar levels?
options: The subarachnoid space is empty above L3
Spinous processes are smaller below L3
The cord ends at about L1-L2
questions.explain: In adults the spinal cord ends at the conus medullaris near L1 or L2, so a needle below this level enters CSF without risk to the cord. The dural sac continues to S2.

open.q: Why is a needle for lumbar puncture in an adult inserted at L3/L4 or L4/L5 rather than at upper lumbar levels?
accept: Cord terminates at the upper lumbar level

questions.q: Why is a chest drain passed just above the upper border of a rib?
options: To avoid the internal thoracic artery
To avoid the long thoracic nerve
questions.explain: The intercostal vein, artery and nerve run in the costal groove along the lower border of each rib. Passing over the upper border of the rib below keeps clear of them.

open.q: Why is a chest drain passed just superior to the upper border of a rib?
accept: Intercostal vessels and nerve run under the rib above
To avoid injuring the costal groove contents
Protect the intercostal nerve and vessels

questions.q: Which muscle forms the anterior axillary fold?
questions.explain: Pectoralis major forms the anterior fold. The posterior fold is made by latissimus dorsi and teres major.

open.q: Which muscle forms the anterior axillary fold?
accept: Muscle forming the anterior border of the axilla

questions.q: Which nerve can be rolled against bone in the groove behind the medial epicondyle of the humerus (funny bone)?
questions.explain: The ulnar nerve lies superficially in the groove behind the medial epicondyle. A knock there causes tingling along the little finger side of the hand.

open.q: Which nerve can be rolled against bone in the groove behind the medial epicondyle of the humerus?
accept: Nerve of the little finger side of the hand
C8 and T1 nerve of the forearm

questions.q: Which carpal bone lies in the floor of the anatomical snuffbox?
questions.explain: The scaphoid is felt in the snuffbox between the tendons of extensor pollicis longus and brevis. Tenderness there after a fall on the outstretched hand suggests a scaphoid fracture.

open.q: Which carpal bone lies in the floor of the anatomical snuffbox?
accept: Carpal bone in the snuffbox floor

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman has night-time tingling of the thumb, index and middle fingers, relieved by shaking the hand. Which structure compresses the nerve?
questions.explain: In carpal tunnel syndrome the median nerve is compressed under the flexor retinaculum (transverse carpal ligament). The ulnar nerve passes through Guyon canal instead.

open.q: A 45-year-old woman has night-time tingling of the thumb, index and middle fingers, relieved by shaking the hand. Which structure compresses the nerve?
accept: Retinaculum on the palmar side of the carpal tunnel

questions.q: With the arm at the side, the inferior angle of the scapula lies level with the spine of which thoracic vertebra?
questions.explain: A line joining the two inferior angles passes through the T7 spinous process, which helps with counting vertebrae and locating the lung bases at the back.

open.q: With the arm at the side, the inferior angle of the scapula lies level with the spine of which thoracic vertebra?

questions.q: A line joining the two posterior superior iliac spines passes through which sacral level?
questions.explain: The skin dimples over the posterior superior iliac spines lie at S2. This is also the level of the lower end of the dural sac.

open.q: A line joining the two posterior superior iliac spines passes through which sacral level?

questions.q: A blow to the side of the head fractures the thin bone at the pterion. Which vessel is most at risk, causing an extradural haematoma?
questions.explain: The anterior branch of the middle meningeal artery lies in a groove behind the pterion. Its rupture causes arterial bleeding between the skull and the dura.

open.q: A blow to the side of the head fractures the thin bone at the pterion. Which vessel is most at risk, causing an extradural haematoma?
accept: Anterior division of the middle meningeal artery
